questions.question: Write the word equation for aerobic respiration and state where, when and in which organisms it takes place. Give three uses of the energy released.
questions.expected_answer: Glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + energy. It takes place in every living cell (mainly in the mitochondria) of every living organism — plants, animals, fungi, bacteria — all the time, day and night. Energy is used for movement, growth, repair, keeping warm, transport across cell membranes, nerve impulses and reproduction (any three).

questions.question: Explain the difference between breathing and respiration, and describe one organism that respires without breathing.
questions.expected_answer: Breathing is a physical process: moving air in and out of the lungs for gas exchange — it supplies oxygen and removes carbon dioxide but releases no energy. Respiration is a chemical process inside cells that releases energy from glucose using oxygen. A plant (or fish, earthworm) has no lungs: oxygen enters through stomata/root surfaces (gills/skin) and every cell respires.

questions.question: Describe an investigation to show that germinating seeds respire, naming the control and the conclusion. Then explain what a green plant does to the gases in the air at night compared with the day.
questions.expected_answer: Living germinating seeds in a sealed flask with a tube of clear limewater, kept in the dark; a control flask with boiled (dead) seeds. After a day the limewater with living seeds turns milky — carbon dioxide produced — while the control stays clear; conclusion: living seeds respire. (A thermometer version shows the living seeds are warmer.) At night a plant only respires, taking in oxygen and giving out carbon dioxide; by day photosynthesis is faster than respiration, so the net effect is carbon dioxide in and oxygen out.
